title: Michael Vargo
text:
Bio
I’m an urban planner, GIS specialist, and data researcher with experience in transportation planning (particularly for transit and active mobility), sustainability initiatives for municipal land use, and data-driven policy evaluation.
I am currently seeking full-time work in private- or public-sector planning or geospatial analysis, having recently completed my Master of City and Regional Planning from The Ohio State University (2024-2026). Explore my extended biography or my portfolio for more information.
Feel free to contact me regarding career opportunities with your organization. I am open to work anywhere in the US or Canada, with preferences for locations in the Great Lakes, Northeast, Pacific Northwest, or Mid-Atlantic states.

title: About Michael Vargo
text:
Michael Vargo is an urban planner, GIS specialist, and data researcher based in Columbus, Ohio.
He has worked at Ohio Department of Transportation in the Division of Planning, where he authored the state’s first comprehensive report on travel forecast accuracy assessment in over a decade. Findings from this assessment, along with technical materials created in support of the work, provide ODOT with a clearer understanding of trends in forecast error. This work dovetailed with research from the Federal Highway Administration into nationwide forecast accuracy, through which he collaborated with contracted research teams on the design and performance of tools for forecast accuracy assessment.
Prior to planning, Michael worked as a high school English language instructor in rural eastern France. He also served as a teaching assistant for a mixed graduate and undergraduate course on transportation and land use during grad school. He greatly enjoys all elements of the teaching process, whether leading instruction, designing coursework, or advising students.
Michael attended the Ohio State University for his Master of City and Regional Planning, along with his Bachelor of Arts in Arabic, French, and Political Science. He also studied at Middlebury Language Schools’ Arabic program.

Research & Interests




Urban Policy

Public housing and its market impacts 
Transit-oriented development 
Urban economics and econometric methods 
Densification and urban core revitalization 
Urban green space and access to natural amenties 
Open-source urban data — OSM and related



Transportation

Active mobility policy and infrastructure planning 
Transit systems and transit-micromobility integration 
Greenways planning and expansion 



Literature, Art, and Culture

Arab and Iranian Sufi poetry and epics 
Links between Sufi and Catholic mystic traditions 
Calligraphic traditions of the Mediterranean 
The works of Simone Weil
Irish contributions to English-language literature 
Art by Maria Helena Vieira da Silva 
Foreign language acquisition and education




Personal
Michael is originally from Columbiana, Ohio, where he grew up on a maple syrup and Christmas tree farm. A fan of the outdoors, he enjoys birding, biking, hiking, and bouldering, and can often be found biking along one of Central Ohio’s many trails.
Michael also loves good espresso, making fun maps, and reading books in new languages (currently Portuguese). Floral button downs, German pop music, and the latest edition of The Economist bring him joy.
